channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Eyes 0.80 as inverse head-and-shoulders breakout holds
item.description: The USD/CHF advances some 0.11% trades near nine-week highs of 0.7991 as risk aversion boosted the Greenback, which has trimmed some earlier losses, to challenge the 0.8000 figure.

item.title: Forex Today: US CPI in focus as US Dollar holds steady amid Middle East war escalation
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades with a cautious tone near the 99.90 region on Tuesday as investors position ahead of Wednesday's highly anticipated United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) report, with inflation expected to tick higher in May.

item.title: Crude Oil shrugs as Trump threatens war over a helicopter
item.description: Trump announced on Tuesday that his military had concluded Iran shot down one of its Apache helicopters over the Strait of Hormuz during the overnight session, and that the US had no choice but to respond. Crude Oil's reaction was to fall.

item.title: Gold price tumbles below $4,250 as Trump vows response to helicopter strike
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) price plunges nearly 2% on Tuesday as tensions in the Middle East escalate afterUS President Donald Trump vowed a response to Iran's downing of a US helicopter near the Strait of Hormuz. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades below $4,250, down 1.93% on the day.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD bears target $60 as selling pressure intensifies
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) tumbles more than 3.5% on Tuesday as price action remains driven by rapidly changing headlines surrounding the Middle East war. At the time of writing, XAG/USD is trading around $65.50, its lowest level since March 23.

item.title: United States Dollar Index rebounds as Middle East peace hopes fade, US inflation data looms
item.description: The United States Dollar Index (DXY) trims earlier losses on Tuesday as traders swing between optimism and caution over a potential US-Iran deal.

item.title: US-Iran nuclear talks near breakthrough on 15-year freeze – NYT
item.description: A New York Times article reports on Tuesday that the US and Iran are close to agreeing on four nuclear themes, according to US officials and diplomats negotiating with Tehran, which could halt Iran’s nuclear program for 15 years or so.

item.title: Gold slides as Trump comments cloud hopes for a Middle East peace deal
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) extends its decline to the lowest level since March on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) rebounds amid uncertainty surrounding a possible end to the war in the Middle East, while a hawkish Federal Reserve (Fed) outlook continues to weigh on the non-yielding metal.

item.title: 18 consecutive months and running: China’s central bank extends Gold-buying spree
item.description: China’s central bank, one of the major Gold purchasers worldwide, continued to add the precious metal to its vaults in April, in a sign that demand from sovereigns remains high.

item.title: US President Trump: US must react to Iranian assault
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump claimed that last night, Iranians shot down a US military Apache helicopter while patrolling the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens despite strong Japanese GDP
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is trading slightly higher on Tuesday as investors digest stronger Japanese growth figures while maintaining a cautious stance ahead of key United States (US) inflation data. The gopher trades near the 160.30 price zone at the time of writing.

item.title: British Pound firms as US CPI countdown tests USD bulls
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) gains 0.31% on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) trims some of its earlier losses amid souring risk appetite, with traders awaiting the release of US inflation figures and tensions in the Middle East, tempered by US President Donald Trump's demand on Israel and Iran.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average futures round-trip rally as chip bounce fades into CPI
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) spent Tuesday proving that a one-day bounce is not the same as a bottom.

item.title: Australian Dollar slips as weak consumer confidence offsets strong China trade data
item.description: The AUD/USD pair falls to near 0.7040 on Tuesday, as the Australian Dollar (AUD) failed to gain support from stronger-than-expected Chinese trade data released earlier in the Asian session.

item.title: Euro gains against US Dollar as Middle East tensions ease, US CPI in focus
item.description: EUR/USD trades on the front foot on Tuesday as tentative signs of de-escalation in the Middle East conflict weigh on safe-haven demand for the US Dollar (USD). Lower Oil prices are also supporting the Euro (EUR), given the Eurozone's heavy reliance on imported energy.

item.title: Canadian Dollar holds steady as Middle East risks, BoC policy uncertainty cap moves
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.3950 on Tuesday at the time of writing after snapping a four-day winning streak.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Stability relies on tighter BI policy – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Enrico Tanuwidjaja and Vincentius Ming Shen note that Indonesia’s FX reserves fell further in May as Bank Indonesia (BI) stepped up interventions to support the Rupiah, which has weakened sharply year-to-date.

item.title: British Pound: Flow-driven gains eye resistance – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Analyst Team notes Sterling is a moderate outperformer versus core majors, supported by broader risk appetite rather than domestic data.

item.title: Canada: Fragile economy under trade and energy strain – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank describes Canada’s economy as fragile, with back-to-back quarterly contractions marking a technical recession and weak investment and trade dragging growth.

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Uptrend against US Dollar intact amid trade surplus – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports that USD/CNH is falling toward support at its June multi-year low as broad Dollar weakness combines with China’s stronger-than-expected trade surplus, driven by AI-related exports and semiconductor imports.

item.title: South Korean Won: Policy support aims to stabilise Won – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Charlie Lay explains that Korean authorities announced new measures to support the Korean Won, including tighter oversight of offshore FX derivatives, scrutiny of suspected misconduct, and expanded FX hedging by the National Pension Service via USD forward selling.

item.title: British Pound gains as report of a BoJ bond-tapering pause weighs on the Japanese Yen
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) strengthens against the Japanese Yen (JPY) on Tuesday as easing tensions in the Middle East support risk-sensitive assets, while the Japanese Yen comes under pressure after Reuters reported that the Bank of Japan (BoJ) is considering pausing its bond-tapering program.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Steady near year-to-date ceiling against USD – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank’s Analyst Team describes USD/CAD as little changed near the top of its year-to-date range, with conditions favouring at least a minor Canadian Dollar rebound as risk sentiment improves.

item.title: Euro: Dependent on Dollar moderation – NBC
item.description: National Bank Canada's (NBC) Stéfane Marion and Kyle Dahms observe that the Euro has softened alongside the broader USD rally, even as Eurozone inflation has reaccelerated and pushed the ECB toward a more hawkish stance.

item.title: Japanese Yen: JGB focus shapes FX outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank's Senior FX Strategist Jane Foley discusses how prospective Bank of Japan (BoJ) policy shifts on JGB purchases and rate hikes could influence the Japanese Yen (JPY).

item.title: Chinese Yuan: Trade data supports currency strength – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale notes China’s trade surplus widened to USD 105.4 billion in May, driven by a 19.4% year‑on‑year surge in exports led by AI‑related equipment.

item.title: Indonesian Rupiah: Off-cycle BI hike to stabilize rupiah – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that USD/IDR retreated sharply after hitting a fresh record high, as Bank Indonesia delivered an unscheduled 25 bps hike to 5.50%, following a surprise 50 bps move in May.

item.title: Canada: Early-stage recovery view – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) economist Claire Fan argues that recent contractions in Canadian GDP do not signal a recession, noting that the C.D. Howe Institute Business Cycle Council shares this view. She emphasizes that sharp swings in population growth distort traditional GDP readings.

item.title: Euro: Safe haven appeal grows with structural boosters – BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas strategists argue that Europe is emerging as an alternative safe haven, with the Euro gaining ground as a global safe asset.

item.title: United States ADP Employment Change 4-week average decreases to 29K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has cooled in late May. The NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, shows that companies added an average of 29K jobs per week in the four weeks ending May 23.
